- File: scripts/write_guard.sh
  Line or code reference: write_guard_sanitize_log_value() (lines 27-35)
  Problem: The function returns early with no output when the sanitized value is empty, producing an empty field in log lines instead of a quoted empty string.
  Why it fails at runtime: When used in command substitution (e.g., `env=$(write_guard_sanitize_log_value "")`), an empty input produces nothing, resulting in log lines like `env=` instead of `env=''`. This creates inconsistency with non-empty values which are shell-escaped with `%q`. Downstream parsers expecting uniformly quoted values may fail to handle the unquoted empty case correctly.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
